roadmap.goal: Epic 5733 slice 01c, ADO Story #5980 — the event pipe. Somebody opens a tab on a Team or Portfolio detail page; the browser chooses a label from a closed list and hands it to Lighthouse's own backend; the backend verifies a live consent grant against its own database on that very request, attaches the four instance facts server-side, and forwards one event to the collector. The maintainer sees it arrive the same day naming the tab and never the Team, revokes from the footer, opens another tab, and watches nothing arrive — with nothing queued anywhere that could outlive the decision. Ships the pipe plus exactly one real product event, `TeamOrPortfolioTabOpened`. DISTILL is committed: 3 acceptance tests are active and green, 31 NUnit cases sit behind `[Ignore]` and 1 Vitest case behind `it.skip`. DELIVER authors no acceptance test — every step below names the pending case(s) it un-skips. The four steps that author anything are the ones DISTILL was structurally unable to write: the browser detector's own specs (a Vitest file cannot statically import a module that does not exist, and `describe.skip` still evaluates its body), the route-key-to-pattern map unit test, and the forwarder's contract unit tests (C# is compiled, so a test naming `UsageDataForwardingService` breaks the whole test assembly's build).

AC-03.2 (the next emit after a revoke does not happen) is the slice's load-bearing criterion and is now asserted at three points: the browser discards its buffer, the gate suppresses at accept, the gate suppresses again at drain. ssot_inputs.design_decisions: Fork 1 — the browser detects, our own backend verifies and forwards; no `posthog-js`, no browser-to-vendor path. Fork 2 — the wire carries closed enumerations and two bounded integers, and NO free `string` property at all, so a customer's entity id reaching the collector is non-representable rather than mitigated. Fork 3 — a bounded in-process channel drained by a hosted service, consent re-checked at drain; no durable outbox, because a durable queue survives the withdrawal it is meant to obey. Fork 4 — a per-token-digest rate limiter with an IP fallback bounds one browser, and a per-instance daily budget that drops silently bounds the maintainer's single collector allowance, which no per-instance limiter can see. Assumption 8 — the single event is a Team or Portfolio detail tab open, chosen because `/teams/:id/:tab?` and `/portfolios/:id/:tab?` are the only routes carrying both a customer entity id that must be dropped and a user-meaningful segment that must be kept.

THE ONE SANCTIONED TEST-FILE EDIT is at 01-05, and DISTILL asked for it in as many words. `UsageDataEventPipeTests.EverythingTheCollectorReceived()` and `UsageDataCollectorAddressTests.TheForwarderHasHadItsChance()` poll on a 5-second `ForwarderBudget` because the integration host does `RemoveAll<IHostedService>()` and the drain therefore never runs there. The fixture summary says: 'The design already names the seam the controller writes to for exactly this reason: give the drain a trigger a test can pull and replace EverythingTheCollectorReceived with it. Polling is the fallback, not the aim.' 01-05 replaces the poll with a trigger. That changes a HELPER, never an assertion. Until 01-05 lands, exactly ONE un-skipped scenario pays wall-clock (`AMessageCarryingARealPageAddress_DoesNotEvenParse` at 01-03, 5s once); from 01-05 onward no scenario pays any.

FOUR STEPS AUTHOR UNIT TESTS, AND EACH IS A GAP DISTILL WAS STRUCTURALLY UNABLE TO CLOSE, not a licence to widen the suite. 01-02 authors the route-key-to-pattern map test (every enum member maps, and no mapped value contains a digit — ADR-190's enforcement row). 01-05 authors the forwarder's contract tests (throw-survival, no-retry, `StopAsync` discards rather than flushes, overflow drops oldest — ADR-190 section 3). 02-01, 02-02 and 02-03 author the browser detector's specs: a Vitest file cannot statically import a module that does not exist, and the import is evaluated before `it.skip` matters, so the module and its specs have to arrive together. Owed coverage, named by DISTILL: the buffer is discarded BEFORE the revoke request is sent; `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` are untouched by buffering; the flush happens on a timer and on `visibilitychange` to hidden; the route key is an enum member and `window.location` is never read; `postEvents` takes the token as a PARAMETER, keeping `UsageDataService` storage-ignorant like its `getState` and `revoke` siblings.

THE MIGRATION IS STEP 01-01 AND NOTHING PRECEDES IT. ADR-191 section 1 adds one nullable `AnalyticsId` column to `UsageDataConsent`. It comes first because every later step reads the pseudonym off that row, because EF InMemory will not warn anybody that the migration is missing (only the sqlite and postgres verify jobs will, at 'Wait for Lighthouse to start'), and because the shared-contract caution applies to an entity that is one release old. Expand-only and additive — NEVER `Recreate`. Use `Lighthouse.Backend/Create-Migration.ps1`, never `dotnet ef migrations add` directly, and run `dotnet restore && dotnet build` over the WHOLE SOLUTION from `Lighthouse.Backend/` first: `dotnet ef` loads the migrations assemblies out of the startup project's output directory, so building only `Lighthouse.Backend.csproj` produces 'Lighthouse.Migrations.Sqlite.dll not found', which means the solution was not built, not that anything is wrong with the model, and copying DLLs into `bin` does not help. Check port 5432 is free — the script starts its own throwaway Postgres container.

`AnyLiveGrantAsync` IS A DELETE AND IT DIES AT 01-04, WITH THE GATE THAT REPLACES IT. ADR-190's reuse verdict: it has no production caller today (the shipped `GetStateAsync` reads `consent?.Decision` directly, and the two `UsageDataConsentServiceTests` setups at :62 and :74 exist to assert the service IGNORES it), and this design removes the only caller it was ever going to have. Its doc comment — 'This is the whole of the question the emitter asks' — becomes false on the day this ships. `PruneStaleAsync` is a KEEP and belongs to slice 02, the slice that makes consent-row growth real. Do NOT plan or write a caller for it here.

THE CI-LEAK GUARD IS NOT OPTIONAL AND BOTH HALVES SHIP TOGETHER. There is exactly one PostHog project and it is the live production census; the free plan allows no second one, and a paid plan would raise the retention floor from one year to seven and falsify the published disclosure. `TeamOrPortfolioTabOpened` fires on ordinary navigation, so every Playwright run that opens a Team or Portfolio tab would emit into the real census with no error and no red build, because emit is fire-and-forget by specification. The guard is CONFIGURATION-shaped: refuse an emit to the compiled-in production default unless `CollectorBaseUrl` was explicitly supplied. The earlier ENVIRONMENT-shaped version was withdrawn and must not be reintroduced — `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` and `DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT` appear in no workflow in this repository, every CI app start launches the published Release binary, and the seventh app start (`ci_verifymacos.yml:145`, `open -a /Applications/Lighthouse.app`) cannot take a per-step override at all. A guard that refuses everything passes `AnInstanceNobodyToldWhereToSend_...` and ships a dead feature, which is precisely why `AnInstanceToldWhereToSend_SendsThere` is un-skipped in the same step.

THREE STEPS TOUCH `Program.cs` — 01-03 (the ingest rate-limit policy and its partition resolver), 01-05 (the hosted service and the queue registration) and 01-06 (the publisher's named client and the collector configuration). Each says so in its notes. A `Program.cs` edit hits the shared-connector whitelist in `ci_changes.yml`, which force-sets every connector output and makes `ci_backend.yml` run the FULL Integration suite — real Jira, Linear, Azure DevOps and ServiceNow calls over the network, on a shared Linear key that rate-limits the next CI run and names the 429 in only one of the resulting failures. Expect higher flake exposure on the pushes that carry those three steps, and do not read a connector failure there as a regression in this slice.

DOCS AND THE COPY CORRECTIONS ARE INSIDE THE DEFINITION OF DONE, not deferred to finalization. This is the standing exception to the project's 'docs wait for the maintainer's confirmation' rule, and the reason is AC-08.2: the shipped consent dialog deliberately carries no field list of its own and links `docs/settings/usagedata.md` as the authoritative account, which makes that page the ONLY place the payload list exists. Shipping the event while the page says 'In this release Lighthouse sends nothing yet' means the product emits data it has told people it does not send, on the very first event. 02-04 removes that block, re-verifies the payload description against what actually shipped rather than against the design it was written from, and fixes the two other places that assert Lighthouse collects nothing.

STRYKER MUTATION TESTING IS NOT A STEP HERE. It is the project's per-feature gate (80% kill rate, both stacks) and runs at feature finalization, after 02-04 and after the maintainer has confirmed the round trip in their own environment. The `mutation/` directory already carries the slice-01a configs; they are gitignored per-feature and will need re-anchoring, because the backend config targets by BYTE OFFSET and the frontend by LINE RANGE, and both shift the moment a line is added.

INTERIM RED IS ACCEPTED, BOUNDED, AND NEVER PUSHED. Commit at every step; push at the slice boundary once the CI-parity gates are green. Two interim states are deliberate and must not be 'fixed' by inventing behaviour early: after 01-03 the ingest endpoint validates and then discards, because the queue arrives at 01-05; after 01-04 the gate mints a permit nothing yet spends. Neither sends anything anywhere, which is the only property that matters while they last.

THE ROUND TRIP IS THE DEMO, AND IT IS A HUMAN TASK WITH NO CRAFTER SURFACE. On the dogfood instance, which is already consenting from slice 01a: open a Team tab, watch the event land at the collector naming the tab and not the Team, revoke from the footer, open another tab, watch nothing land. Same day. Tracked by the orchestrator, not by a step. An empty collector dashboard in the weeks AFTER this ships is the expected state, not a broken pipe — the unprompted ask is slice 02 (#5835), so until then the consenting population is the dogfood instance plus whoever went looking for the footer icon.

TWO DELIVER-OWNED OPEN QUESTIONS ARE CARRIED FORWARD AND ARE NOT STEPS. Confirm which generic path patterns EasyPrivacy and AdGuard actually carry and check `usagedata/events` against them — those lists match on any domain, not only vendor ones, so a route named for tracking would reintroduce at larger scale the exact ad-blocker bias this whole design exists to avoid. And recompute the PostHog free-tier headroom at the new per-event volume before #5837 picks its event set; ADR-176's ~30k events/month was a heartbeat estimate and is now wrong by orders of magnitude, and a paid plan would widen retention to seven years and falsify the published position. Both are checks the maintainer makes, not code a crafter writes.

ONE PRE-AUTHORISED ADDITION TO THE DESIGN COMPONENT TABLE: `Lighthouse.Frontend/src/App.tsx` gains a single call to the detector hook, beside the existing `<Footer />` and `<SurveyNudge />`. The table names modules rather than call sites, and the detector needs a mount point inside the Router context. This is not a deviation a crafter discovered; it is recorded here so the orchestrator does not stop on it.
out_of_scope: Every further named product event. This slice ships exactly ONE — `TeamOrPortfolioTabOpened`. The remaining 1-3 belong to slice 04 (#5837), informed by the uptake number slice 02 produces. A second enum member here would make `EveryEventTheProductCanSend_HasALineOnThePage` fail against a page that describes one event, which is the disclosure gate working as designed.
The unprompted consent dialog and any re-ask cadence — slice 02 (#5835). The dialog still opens only when somebody clicks the footer indicator.

The admin master switch and its premium gating — slice 03 (#5836). The gate READS the optional feature from the start, so 03 is a seed and a toggle rather than new enforcement; do not build the toggle here.

Scheduling `PruneStaleAsync`. It is a KEEP with zero production callers and it is OWNED BY SLICE 02 — the slice that makes consent-row growth real. Adding a caller here would take work that belongs to the slice that creates the problem.

Deleting the `UsageData:InstanceId` rows already written on granting instances. ADR-191 section 6 is explicit: they are sixteen random bytes that nothing reads and that identify nothing, and they are deliberately NOT added to `AppSettingSeeder.RemoveObsoleteSettings`, which deletes by `Id` — every row minted through that path carries the default `Id = 0`, so naming a low id in that sweep would take unrelated rows with it. `AppSettingSeeder` is UNCHANGED.

Any cache in front of the gate. ADR-190 section 2 answers the question ADR-174 deferred: still no cache, because the number is not there — a browser flushes at most twice a minute and the gate is one read on a unique index. If one is ever added it goes INSIDE the gate and may only ever SUPPRESS, never permit.

A durable outbox, a persisted queue, or a browser-side queue in `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`. The right property for this queue is that it FORGETS: a durable queue survives a revocation and sends afterwards, which is exactly what AC-03.2 forbids, and it would put unsent analytics about customer behaviour into the customer's own database.
Retrying a failed publish. ADR-190 section 3: none. A retry is a second chance to send something whose consent may have changed in the meantime, and a usage event that is lost costs nothing.
Flushing the queue on shutdown. `StopAsync` DISCARDS. Flushing would mean sending after the last chance to check consent, and would put a vendor's latency on a container's shutdown path.

Constant-time work on the ingest path to close the timing side-channel. It is real, it is named in ADR-190 section 2, it is the same residual the shipped `/state` endpoint already carries in its own comment, and it is bounded by the rate limiter rather than closed — constant-time work would be disproportionate for a pseudonymous analytics endpoint.

Validating the consent token's SHAPE, or answering `400` for a malformed one. This is the rule most likely to be helpfully broken by someone adding a guard clause, so it is stated rather than left implicit: `400` is reserved for a malformed BODY. An empty, truncated, over-long or non-base64url token fails to resolve and lands on the same `204` as a token that was never minted. The moment a malformed token is answered differently, the endpoint becomes an oracle for token shape, and shape plus a rate limit is where guessing starts.
An RBAC permission on the ingest endpoint. The consent token IS the authorisation, and on an auth-off instance there is no role to check.

Any Playwright work. No E2E spec, no page object, no `@screenshot` regeneration. The slice-01a walking skeleton stands; the round trip for this slice is the dogfood demo, which is a human task. E2E minimalism applies and no scenario in this slice needs a browser to prove anything the integration fixtures cannot.
Making the collector endpoint customer-configurable beyond the `CollectorBaseUrl` it already has, and any Helm chart change. `app.usageData.collectorBaseUrl` is the chart's existing key.

The privacy canary workflow (`ci_usagedata_canary.yml`) and the `force_full` filter change that has to precede it. Those are DEVOPS-owned and land on their own schedule; the guard this slice ships is the configuration-shaped refusal, which needs no YAML at all.
Stryker mutation testing, docs screenshots, website copy and the ADO transition. Feature finalization owns all four, after the maintainer confirms the round trip.

Editing, weakening, reordering or adding to any assertion in the six DISTILL-authored test files. Removing an `[Ignore]` or a `.skip` is the only permitted edit, with the single helper exception recorded in maintainer_decisions.

phases.name: Slice 01c backend — accept, gate, drain, send
phases.description: The pipe, built in the only order that never leaves a commit in which the instance sends where it should not: first the pseudonym the events will be counted under, then a wire with no field a path could travel in, then an endpoint that is anonymous, non-oracular and actually limited, then the fail-closed gate, then the queue and the forwarder with a trigger a test can pull instead of a five-second wait, then the publisher together with the refusal to send where nobody pointed it, then the four instance facts, then the daily budget. Eight steps, 29 of the 31 pending NUnit cases.

steps.implementation_notes:
WHY THERE IS NO PENDING CASE TO UN-SKIP, stated rather than glossed. DT-3 forbids a backend test naming a type or member that does not exist: C# is compiled, so a pending test naming `AnalyticsId` would break the whole test assembly's build, which is BROKEN rather than pending and trips the zero-warning gate besides. What DISTILL could write about this column, it wrote as an ACTIVE test — `TheValueThatTellsARepeatVisitFromANewOne_NeverCrossesTheWire` asserts the complete field set of both browser-facing answers, and it is deliberately not ignored because it can be broken today: the way the pseudonym would reach the wire is somebody adding it to the browser's own answer for convenience, under a name nobody thought to forbid. That test is this step's gate, and it must be green before and after.

WHAT THIS STEP DOES — two commits.

COMMIT 1, the deletion. Remove `IAppSettingService.EnsureUsageDataInstanceId()` (:41) and `GetUsageDataInstanceId()` (:47), their implementations in `AppSettingService` (:101 and :148), the `AppSettingKeys.UsageDataInstanceId` constant (:27), and the call site with its whole try/catch at `UsageDataConsentService.cs:76-88`. Delete the shipped tests that covered them in `AppSettingServiceTest.cs` (from :258). Removing the call site removes `UsageDataConsentService`'s reason to hold `IAppSettingService` at all — drop the constructor parameter and the mock in `UsageDataConsentServiceTests.CreateService()` (:209-214) with it. `AppSettingSeeder` is UNCHANGED and deliberately not extended.

COMMIT 2, the column and its migration. Add `public string? AnalyticsId { get; set; }` to `UsageDataConsent`. NO CLR initializer — not `= string.Empty`, not anything. A non-type-default initializer on a persisted property makes EF treat it as the property sentinel and the model-differ never reconciles it, which is a documented trap in this repository that produced perpetual 'pending model changes'. Nullable is also the correct semantics: null for every refusal, every withdrawal, and every row already in the table. Mint it in `RecordDecisionAsync` inside the SAME `AddAsync` that writes the consent row, only when `decision == UsageDataDecision.Granted`, via `UrlSafeValue.Generate(16)` — the same helper the shipped token path already uses, and it takes no inputs, which is what makes 'derived from nothing' visible rather than asserted. There is no second table, no get-or-create, no unique-violation catch and no ordering problem; those were the three most fragile parts of the superseded design and they disappear with the shared scalar.

THE MIGRATION, in this exact order: `cd Lighthouse.Backend` then `dotnet restore` then `dotnet build` over the WHOLE SOLUTION (not just Lighthouse.Backend.csproj) then `pwsh ./Create-Migration.ps1 -MigrationName AddUsageDataAnalyticsId`. Never `dotnet ef migrations add` directly — the script does sqlite plus a throwaway-Postgres-container pass, and both providers must get the migration. Never `Recreate`; migrations in this repository are additive and expand-only per release, so an image rollback stays a supported recovery path. `dotnet ef` loads the migrations assemblies out of the STARTUP project's output directory, so if you skip the solution build you get 'Assets file ... not found' or 'Lighthouse.Migrations.Sqlite.dll not found' — both mean the solution was not built into the backend's output directory, NOT that anything is wrong with your model, and copying DLLs into `bin` does not help. Check port 5432 is free first; the script starts its own container on it. If `has-pending-model-changes` disagrees with a snapshot that visibly contains the change, force `dotnet build <MigrationsProject>.csproj --no-incremental` — the tool reads the compiled snapshot, not the .cs.

VERIFY BEFORE MOVING ON, because the InMemory test provider will not warn you and only the sqlite and postgres verify jobs will, at 'Wait for Lighthouse to start': run the app with `Database__Provider=sqlite` against a throwaway file and confirm it reaches 'Application started' with no `PendingModelChangesWarning`.

SHARED-CONTRACT CAUTION. `UsageDataConsent` is one release old and is constructed in eight places across production and tests. Grep for `new UsageDataConsent` and extend the local `Consent(...)` helper at `UsageDataConsentRepositoryTests.cs:213` BEFORE touching the entity — there is no shared test factory, and that helper is the closest thing to one.

STANDING GUARDS: `dotnet build` zero warnings under `TreatWarningsAsErrors`; `dotnet test --filter "TestCategory!=Integration&TestCategory!=JiraIntegration&TestCategory!=LinearIntegration&TestCategory!=AdoIntegration&TestCategory!=ServiceNowIntegration"` green; `cd Lighthouse.Backend && dotnet format analyzers Lighthouse.sln --severity info --verify-no-changes --no-restore` clean over the files this step touched, with the filter unioning `git diff --name-only` and `git status --porcelain` so new files are not invisible to it. Sonar analyzer rules that now FAIL the build: CA1861, CA1859, CA1825, CA2016, NUnit1028, NUnit2045, NUnit2056 — generated migration files keep them advisory, and hand-editing generated code is not the fix for any of them. No file outside `files_to_modify` touched.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: this project is C# .NET 10 plus React/TypeScript, not the Python/Hypothesis pilot — the ATDD infrastructure policy says so in its own preamble, and the C#/TS rows of the polyglot matrix govern. The compensating rigour here is that the column's one observable property (it is never on the wire, in either direction) is pinned by an ACTIVE black-box assertion over the complete field set of both browser-facing answers, rather than by the absence of one field under a name somebody remembered to forbid.

steps.implementation_notes:
WHAT THIS STEP DOES — the whole enforcement of the route-pattern requirement, and it is structural rather than defensive. Declare `UsageDataEventName` with exactly one member (`TeamOrPortfolioTabOpened`) and `UsageDataRouteKey` whose members are (entity type, tab) pairs — `TeamDetail_Metrics`, `PortfolioDetail_Settings` and their siblings, derived from `App.tsx:213,218` (`/teams/:id/:tab?` and `/portfolios/:id/:tab?`). Declare `UsageDataEventBatchDto` carrying `UsageDataEventDto[]`, each with `Name`, `Route`, `OffsetMs` and `Sequence` and NOTHING ELSE. Declare `UsageDataRoutePatterns` as the key-to-pattern map, so the pattern the collector eventually sees is a literal we own.

A CLIENT THAT SENDS `/teams/42` IS NOT NORMALISED — IT DOES NOT DESERIALISE, because that string is not a member of the enum. There is no regex whose completeness the promise depends on, and no moment at which a real entity id exists inside our own process to be copied out by request logging or an exception message on the way past. Do not add a normaliser, an allow-list or a sanitiser; each would reintroduce the arrival the enum makes impossible.

BOTH ENUMS ARE VALUE TYPES ON A `[FromBody]` DTO, so every one is declared NULLABLE with the absent case rejected explicitly at the read site. `csharpsquid:S6964` has fired on this exact shape three times in this repository. The fix that is NOT available is `[JsonRequired]`: adding it to a new property makes every payload written before it return `400`. Nullable plus an explicit check is the house answer, and it is also what makes `AMessageMissingAPart_IsRefusedRatherThanGuessed` mean something — zero is a real member of both enums, so a whole-number field left out of a message would otherwise be read as naming something nobody sent.

THE MAP TEST, authored here. ADR-190's enforcement table asks for it and DISTILL could not write it, because a test naming `UsageDataRoutePatterns` would not compile before the type existed. Two assertions: every declared `UsageDataRouteKey` member has a mapping, and no mapped value contains a digit. The second is the one that catches somebody 'helpfully' mapping a key to a concrete address.

THE TWO ARCHUNIT RULES. `NothingSentOrReceivedOnThisPath_HasAFieldThatCouldHoldFreeText` inspects public types whose names start with `UsageDataEvent`; that set is EMPTY today, so the rule currently forbids nothing and its own first assertion says so. Un-skipping it here takes it from red-on-an-empty-set to green over the real message types, which is the honest transition. `NothingOnTheEmitPath_BuildsItsOwnWayOut` inspects source files named `*UsageData*`, a set that is already non-empty, so it may go GREEN THE MOMENT IT IS UN-SKIPPED. Prove it can fail before trusting it — and do that by SUBSTITUTION, never by commenting a call out: deleting a guarded call leaves a constructor parameter unread (CS9113, an error under `TreatWarningsAsErrors`), and neutralising an `if` by leaving a bare block trips S1199, also error-severity here. Temporarily add `new HttpClient()` to one usage-data source file, watch the rule name it, remove it.

ARCHUNIT FLUENT SLICE FIELDS MUST BE CONCRETE `GivenTypesConjunctionWithDescription`, not an interface — CA1859 fails the Sonar gate on that shape and has fired six times at once in one such file.

STANDING GUARDS: as 01-01, plus — the DTO gains no `string` property now or ever; S1192 (the same literal three or more times in one file) is the usual casualty of declaring a vocabulary, so give any repeated sentence a `private const` when you write it rather than after CI says so; SYSLIB1045 forbids `new Regex(...)` — prefer no regex at all here, which the enum already makes possible. steps.name: The ingest endpoint: anonymous, non-oracular, and actually limited
criteria: `POST /api/latest/usagedata/events` is anonymous, takes the consent token in `X-Lighthouse-UsageData-Token`, and answers `204` with an empty body in every case except a malformed body, which is `400`
A body naming a route that is a real page address, or an event this release does not declare, is a `400` and forwards nothing
A body missing a field, carrying an out-of-range enum ordinal, an impossible offset, or text that is not a message at all is refused with a status below 500 — the instance never falls over
`UsageDataIngestPolicy` is declared in `RateLimitingConfiguration` AND configured in `appsettings.json` in the same commit, and resolves to a real limiter rather than `NoLimiter`
The limiter partitions on the digest of the presented token with a client-IP fallback, so two browsers behind one office address do not spend each other's allowance

WHAT THIS STEP DOES — adds the `POST events` action to the shipped `UsageDataController`, which is already `[AllowAnonymous]` for the reason its class comment gives, and bounds it in the same commit.

THE ANSWER IS `204` IN EVERY CASE, PERMITTED OR NOT, with an empty body. The endpoint must not tell a caller whether the token it presented is real; that is the same non-oracle rule `DELETE /consent` already follows at :83-86 and for the same reason. A malformed BODY is the one exception and answers `400`, because that is a bug in our own client, not a probe. Do NOT validate the token's shape and do NOT `400` on a bad one — see the out_of_scope entry; that rule is the one a guard clause would helpfully break.

THE POLICY IS DECLARED AND CONFIGURED IN THE SAME COMMIT, and this is not tidiness. `ConfigureRateLimiting` returns `RateLimitPartition.GetNoLimiter("unconfigured")` for a policy name that has no entry in configuration (`Program.cs:1159-1162`), silently — so a policy declared in `RateLimitingConfiguration` and forgotten in `appsettings.json` ships an UNLIMITED anonymous write endpoint that looks limited in the source. Name the constant `UsageDataIngestPolicy` with the configuration key `UsageDataIngest`, which is what the ceiling fixture configures. The shipped `UsageDataConsent` policy — 20 / 60s / queue 0 at `appsettings.json:68` — is the reference shape.

THE PARTITION KEY IS THE TOKEN DIGEST, NOT THE IP. `ResolvePartitionKey(httpContext)` is shared by the existing policies and resolves to the client address; the ingest policy needs its own resolver that hashes the `X-Lighthouse-UsageData-Token` header and falls back to the client address when no token is present. Fifty colleagues behind one corporate NAT share an address and would throttle each other, which would silence exactly the busiest instances — the ones worth hearing from. The digest is computed from the header with NO database read, so it costs nothing at the limiter.

THIS STEP EDITS `Program.cs`, which hits the shared-connector whitelist in `ci_changes.yml` and forces the full backend Integration suite on the push that carries it. That is not a regression in this slice.

Do not widen the budget and do not shorten it; replace it when there is something to pull.

steps.name: The fail-closed gate, and suppression counted rather than logged
criteria: The gate resolves the presented token through `FindByTokenHashAsync`, permits only a `Granted` row inside the liveness window, refreshes `LastSeenAt` through the existing throttled `TouchAsync`, and consults no cache

Every uncertainty resolves to do-not-forward: an absent token, an unknown token, a declined or revoked row, a stale row, a throwing repository, a cancellation — the gate never throws into a user's request
A malformed token is answered byte-identically to an unknown one, and neither is a `400`

A browser that withdrew and keeps flushing produces no log line per flush — suppression is counted per reason and reported once a day, at Debug for policy outcomes and Warning for `EvaluationFailed` and `BudgetExhausted`

`AnyLiveGrantAsync` is gone from the interface, the implementation and its four shipped tests, and the two `UsageDataConsentServiceTests` setups that existed to assert the service ignored it are gone with it
steps.scenario_name: UN-SKIPS 4 pending cases: `AMalformedToken_IsAnsweredExactlyAsAnUnknownOneIs` (empty | truncated | wrong alphabet) | `ABrowserThatWithdrewAndKeepsFlushing_AddsNoLinePerFlush`.
steps.implementation_notes:
WHAT THIS STEP DOES — the enforcement point. The frontend cannot be it: whatever endpoint the browser posts to is anonymous, authentication is optional in Lighthouse and impossible in standalone, and with it off every caller shares the subject `lighthouse|auth-disabled`. Hiding a button is a decision about a screen. This is the only place an answer can actually be enforced, so it assumes its caller is hostile and checks on every request.

ONE INDEXED READ, NO CACHE, AND THE REASON IS AN ABSENT NUMBER RATHER THAN A PRINCIPLE. A browser flushes at most twice a minute; the lookup rides the unique `TokenHash` index at `LighthouseAppContext.cs:166-168`, the same read the shipped state endpoint already performs hourly from every open tab. There is no cost to avoid, and the only failure a cache could buy is sending after a revoke. If one is ever added it goes INSIDE the gate and may only ever SUPPRESS.

THE PERMIT. `UsageDataEmitPermit` is sealed and gate-minted, and the publisher requires one — no zero-argument overload. This prevents emission BY OMISSION; it is not a compile-time guarantee, because there is one assembly and `InternalsVisibleTo` exists. The ArchUnit rule is what carries the rest, and ADR-174's own correction on this point is inherited verbatim rather than quietly upgraded.

`UsageDataSuppressionReason` is closed: `MasterSwitchOff`, `NoLiveConsent`, `RateLimited`, `BudgetExhausted`, `EvaluationFailed`. `NoInstanceIdentifier` is DROPPED — there is no instance identifier any more.

SUPPRESSION IS COUNTED, NOT LOGGED, and this INVERTS the superseded rule on purpose. ADR-174 allowed 'at most one log line per attempt', which was right for one attempt a day and becomes a flood mechanism at per-event granularity: a revoked browser with a stale tab open would emit a suppression line every flush, forever, and the instance most likely to fill a disk is the one whose owner already withdrew. One line per reason per day, Debug for `NoLiveConsent` and `MasterSwitchOff`, Warning for `EvaluationFailed` and `BudgetExhausted`. `EvaluationFailed` is the one an operator must be able to FIND, because it is the only reason that means the feature is broken rather than switched off. Note the shape the test uses: it counts lines mentioning 'usage' ACROSS EVERY LEVEL including Verbose, because demoting a line to Debug does not stop it filling a disk.

THE GATE READS THE MASTER SWITCH FROM THE START. The optional feature does not exist until slice 03; read it, default to on, and do not build the toggle. That is what makes 03 a seed rather than new enforcement.

DO NOT COPY `useRbac`. A crafter meets it within a few files of this one and it fails OPEN on purpose, via `PERMISSIVE_SUMMARY`. This gate fails CLOSED.

THE DELETION. `AnyLiveGrantAsync` goes from `IUsageDataConsentRepository.cs:44` and `UsageDataConsentRepository.cs:51`, with the four `AnyLiveGrantAsync_*` tests in `UsageDataConsentRepositoryTests.cs` (from :134) and the two `UsageDataConsentServiceTests` setups at :62 and :74. It dies HERE rather than at 01-01 because this is the step a reader learns why: it was the heartbeat's gate, there is no heartbeat, and its doc comment — 'This is the whole of the question the emitter asks' — becomes false on the day this ships. `PruneStaleAsync` STAYS and belongs to slice 02; do not give it a caller.

THE THREE MALFORMED-TOKEN CASES MAY GO GREEN THE MOMENT THEY ARE UN-SKIPPED, because 01-03 already answers `204` to everything. Prove they can fail before trusting them, and do it by substitution: make the gate `400` on an empty token, watch all three name it, revert. Never by deleting a call or blanking an `if` — CS9113 and S1199 are both errors here.

INTERIM STATE, DELIBERATE: the permit has no consumer until 01-05.

THIS STEP TOUCHES `Program.cs` only for the DI registration of `IUsageDataGate`, which it does. Say so in the commit body; the full-Integration-suite consequence applies.

STANDING GUARDS: as 01-01, plus — S2139 forbids log-and-rethrow where a higher layer already logs, which is exactly the shape a fail-closed gate invites; S6667 requires a catch that logs to pass the caught exception as the FIRST argument, and it is error-severity here; CA1859 judges non-public members, so a private helper returning `IReadOnlyList<T>` for a `List<T>` fails the Sonar gate while the local build stays silent. No assertion edited; the only permitted diff to `UsageDataEventPipeTests.cs` is the `[Ignore]` attributes.

steps.name: The queue and the forwarder, with a trigger a test can pull
criteria: An accepted batch goes onto a bounded in-process channel behind `IUsageDataEventQueue`; nothing is persisted, and overflow drops rather than blocking the request thread

`UsageDataForwardingService` is a plain `BackgroundService` that drains the channel, re-checks consent at drain keyed on the token hash the batch carries, and touches no repository, no `DbContext` and no domain-event dispatcher
A publish that throws is caught and counted and the loop continues; a failed publish is never retried; `StopAsync` discards what is still queued rather than flushing it
The three integration fixtures pull a trigger instead of polling, and no scenario in the suite spends the five-second forwarder budget again
`ThePartThatSends_TouchesNothingBeyondWhatIsWaitingAndTheWayOut` is green over a forwarder that actually exists
steps.scenario_name: UN-SKIPS 1 pending case: `ThePartThatSends_TouchesNothingBeyondWhatIsWaitingAndTheWayOut`. ALSO AUTHORS the forwarder-contract unit tests ADR-190 section 3's enforcement rows require and DT-3 forbade DISTILL from writing: the loop survives a publisher that throws on every call | one batch produces exactly one publish attempt | `StopAsync` leaves the publisher uncalled | the channel drops rather than blocking on overflow. ALSO REPLACES the polling helper with the trigger DISTILL asked for by name.
steps.implementation_notes:
WHAT THIS STEP DOES — the thing that makes the revocation window shut, and the thing that makes the whole suite stop paying wall-clock.

THE FORWARDER HAS A CONTRACT, NOT A DESCRIPTION, and ADR-190 section 3 states it as a table. Type: `UsageDataForwardingService : BackgroundService`, registered with `AddHostedService` — the house precedent for instance-scoped background work is `GracefulShutdownService` and `KeyRingFileWatcher`, NOT `UpdateServiceBase`, which is per-entity and queue-backed and has no entity to iterate here. Contract shape: bounded-change. Universe: the `Channel<UsageDataEventBatch>` it reads and one named `HttpClient`, and NOTHING ELSE — it writes no database row, publishes no domain event and touches no other service's state. Declared delta: the channel empties and the collector receives zero or more events. Retry: NONE. Failure: never escapes the loop; an exception that ended the drain loop would silently stop usage data for the process lifetime. Shutdown: cooperative and non-blocking; whatever is still queued is DISCARDED. Cycle: drains continuously with a short idle wait, and the interval is not load-bearing — it bounds the accept-to-drain revocation window, so shorter is strictly better and the only cost is wake-ups.

THE GATE RUNS AGAIN AT DRAIN, keyed on the token hash the queued batch carries. That is the half a mocked queue would silently drop: a revocation that commits between accept and drain must suppress the batch, and that is one more indexed read per drain cycle. Note the honest limit, which is a documented residual rather than a test: a batch already handed to `HttpClient` when the revoke commits will complete. One in-flight request, single-digit hundreds of milliseconds. No design that sends over a network closes it.

NOTHING IS PERSISTED. No outbox table, no browser-side queue. That is not laziness, it is the answer to 'what happens to queued events when consent is revoked mid-flight' — a durable queue survives the revocation and sends afterwards, which is precisely what AC-03.2 forbids. It would also put unsent analytics about customer behaviour into the customer's own database, which is a new category of thing for an operator to reason about.

THE TRIGGER, WHICH IS THE SANCTIONED TEST-FILE EDIT. `TestWebApplicationFactory` does `RemoveAll<IHostedService>()`, so the drain does not run inside the integration host at all — which is why `EverythingTheCollectorReceived()` and `TheForwarderHasHadItsChance()` currently sit on a five-second Stopwatch loop, and why the fixture summary says in as many words: give the drain a trigger a test can pull and replace the helper with it. Expose the drain as a method on the seam the controller writes to (or a thin drainer the hosted service merely calls in a loop), and rewrite the two helpers to pull it and return. This changes a HELPER; it changes no assertion, no scenario name and no expected value. After this step, a negative scenario that asserts nothing was sent costs microseconds instead of five seconds, and a loaded build agent no longer decides whether the suite is honest.

THE FOUR CONTRACT TESTS ARE AUTHORED HERE and are the same class of owed work as the browser specs: DT-3 made them unwritable in DISTILL, because a test naming `UsageDataForwardingService` breaks the whole test assembly's build. Keep them proportionate — four scenarios, each an enforcement row of ADR-190 section 3, using a counting and a throwing publisher double.

THE ARCHUNIT RULE inspects types whose names contain both `UsageData` and `Forward` and forbids any dependency on `Lighthouse.Backend.Data.`, on anything named `Repository`, or on `IDomainEventDispatcher`. Note the recorded trap: an ArchUnit dependency on a type used only inside an `async` method passes in Debug and FAILS in Release, so run this rule in Release before trusting it.

THIS STEP EDITS `Program.cs` — `AddHostedService<UsageDataForwardingService>()` and the queue registration. Full backend Integration suite consequence applies; say so in the commit body.

THE REPLICA PROBLEM DISSOLVES RATHER THAN BEING SOLVED, and nobody should reintroduce a day key to solve it. A plain `AddHostedService` runs in every replica, which mattered when three replicas would emit three heartbeats a day under one identifier. A browser-originated event enters through exactly ONE replica's ingest endpoint and is forwarded once by that replica. `UpdateQueueService` and `IUpdateExecutionLock` are not needed, and this time the conclusion follows from the reason.

STANDING GUARDS: as 01-01, plus — CA1869 (cache `JsonSerializerOptions` in a static readonly field, never `new` one per call) bites hardest in one-line test helpers written while fixing something else, and this step writes test helpers that touch JSON: grep the new test file for `new JsonSerializerOptions` before committing. NUnit2045 is about the METHOD, not the test — two `Assert.That` calls inside a private helper are flagged even when every caller wraps the helper in `Assert.EnterMultipleScope()`. CA1806 — a `Try*` whose boolean is discarded — is INFO locally and fails the gate; grep every `Try` in your own diff.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: C#/.NET project; integration tests verify wiring and remain single-example. The compensating rigour is that the forwarder's universe is asserted STRUCTURALLY by ArchUnit rather than by example, which is the closest this stack gets to a quantified claim about what a component may touch.

steps.name: The publisher, and the refusal to send where nobody pointed it
criteria: One file, and only one, names the collector host; every event carries `$ip: null` and `$geoip_disable: true` in the message itself
A Team tab opened on a consenting browser reaches the collector naming the tab, and matching `/teams/[0-9]` nowhere in what was sent

A browser that refused, a caller with no consent behind it, and an instance nobody has answered on each reach the collector not once — and a withdrawal stops the very next batch, and the batch already waiting, without a restart and without a cycle boundary
An instance nobody told where to send does not fall back to the compiled-in default, and says so at Warning where an operator would find it
An instance told where to send actually sends there — the guard refuses a default, not everything
steps.scenario_name: UN-SKIPS 9 pending cases. From `UsageDataEventPipeTests`: `ATabOpenedOnATeam_ReachesTheCollectorNamingTheTabAndNeverTheTeam` | `ABrowserThatRefused_SendsNothingEvenThoughItHoldsAToken` | `ACallerWithNoConsentBehindIt_SendsNothingHoweverWellFormedItsMessageIs` | `ABrowserThatChangedItsMind_SendsNothingOnItsVeryNextEvent` | `AWithdrawalWhileABatchIsStillWaiting_StopsThatBatchToo` | `AnInstanceNobodyHasAnsweredOn_ReachesTheCollectorNotOnce`. From `UsageDataCollectorAddressTests`: `AnInstanceNobodyToldWhereToSend_DoesNotSendToTheLiveCensusAndSaysWhyNot` | `AnInstanceToldWhereToSend_SendsThere`. From `UsageDataEmitSeamArchUnitTest`: `TheAddressTheDataGoesTo_IsWrittenDownInExactlyOnePlace`.
steps.implementation_notes:
THIS IS THE LARGEST STEP IN THE ROADMAP AND IT CANNOT BE CUT, which is worth saying before the criteria are read. Nothing on the forward side is observable until something forwards, so every one of those nine cases becomes assertable at exactly this commit and not before. The splits that suggest themselves all leave a commit in which the instance sends where it must not: a publisher without the address guard can fall back to the live census; a publisher without the drain-time re-check sends a batch accepted before a withdrawal. Neither may exist for even one commit.

WHAT THIS STEP DOES — `PostHogUsageDataPublisher` on a NAMED `HttpClient` from `IHttpClientFactory`, posting to `{CollectorBaseUrl}/i/v0/e/`, with the collector host as a single constant in this one file so an architecture rule has a name to point at. `$ip: null` and `$geoip_disable: true` ride EVERY event, in the message itself, so the promise does not depend on a setting in somebody else's console staying where it was. The route key is translated to its pattern here, through the map declared at 01-02 — the browser sent a label, and this is where that label becomes the `/teams/:id` string the collector sees.

THE GUARD, BOTH DIRECTIONS, AND IT IS CONFIGURATION-SHAPED. Refuse an emit to the compiled-in production default unless `CollectorBaseUrl` was EXPLICITLY SUPPLIED. There is exactly one PostHog project and it is the live census the maintainer reads; the free plan allows no second one, and a paid plan would raise the retention floor from one year to seven and falsify a disclosure that commits us to re-asking every consenting person about a material change. `TeamOrPortfolioTabOpened` fires on ordinary navigation and the browser tests open Team and Portfolio tabs constantly, so without this guard every CI run would invent events in the real numbers — silently, with no error and no red build, because sending degrades without complaint by specification. A real deployment always supplies the value: the chart renders it, Docker and standalone set it. No CI app start does, including `ci_verifymacos.yml:145`, which launches an installed bundle and cannot take a per-step override at all — which is exactly why the invariant is configuration-shaped rather than environment-shaped.

DO NOT REINTRODUCE THE ENVIRONMENT-SHAPED VERSION. It was withdrawn on the evidence: `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` and `DOTNET_ENVIRONMENT` appear in NO workflow in this repository, and every app start launches the published Release binary, which defaults to Production. It would never have fired in any environment it was written for.

REFUSING QUIETLY LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE WORKING. A usage event dropping silently is normal here by design, so the refusal must say so at Warning, where somebody running an instance that cannot send would find it. Distinguish 'not configured' from 'configured and unreachable'; only the first refuses.

A GUARD THAT REFUSES EVERYTHING PASSES THE FIRST SCENARIO AND SHIPS A DEAD FEATURE. That is why `AnInstanceToldWhereToSend_SendsThere` is un-skipped in this same step and why the fixture's own summary says both halves are there on purpose: nothing else in the suite would notice a permanently silent pipe, because everything else asserts that things do NOT get sent. Treat 'empty' as never sufficient evidence — the fixture's active positive control, `NothingWasSent_IsSomethingThisFixtureCanActuallyTell`, exists for the same reason and must stay green.

THE ONE-FILE RULE. `TheAddressTheDataGoesTo_IsWrittenDownInExactlyOnePlace` counts production source files containing the string 'posthog', case-insensitively, and asserts exactly ONE. It currently fails with zero. A second mention — in a comment, in a configuration default written somewhere else, in a log message — fails it just as hard, and that is the rule working: spread out, there is no single answer to where this data goes and nothing for the no-hand-built-clients rule to be about.

NEVER BUILD AN `HttpClient` BY HAND on this path. The whole zero-leak assertion sits in front of the clients the framework hands out; a client built here goes out through a pipeline nothing is watching, and the assertion that an instance without consent contacts nobody quietly stops covering it. The 01-02 ArchUnit rule is what holds this, and the two ship together or neither is worth having.

THIS STEP EDITS `Program.cs` — `AddHttpClient` for the named client and the publisher registration. Full backend Integration suite consequence applies.

STANDING GUARDS: as 01-01, plus — CA1869 for the serializer options this file will need; SYSLIB1045 forbids `new Regex(...)`; the publisher must never resolve for real in any other test, which the ATDD policy states as a rule ('a test may never let the real publisher resolve') and the `.invalid` addresses in the fixtures enforce. No assertion edited in any of the three test files.

The compensating rigour is the `OutboundRequestRecordingFilter`, which sits in front of EVERY client the framework hands out and records address and body — so 'nothing was sent' is something a test can see rather than something it infers from a double that was not called.

steps.name: The instance facts, attached here and never asked of the browser
criteria: Every forwarded event carries version, deployment mode, licence tier and auth-enabled, resolved server-side from `ILighthouseReleaseService`, `IPlatformService`, `ILicenseService` and `IAuthModeResolver`
A version that does not match the shape of a published release is emitted as the literal `unreleased`, and a test host is exactly such a build
The deployment-mode resolver composes `IPlatformService` and returns a closed value set, with Kubernetes distinguished from Docker although `IsDocker()` is true in a pod
None of the four facts is a field in any request or response the browser can see or set
`TheFactsAboutTheInstance_AreAddedHereAndNeverAskedOfTheBrowser` is green, including its `$ip` and geoip assertions
steps.implementation_notes:
WHAT THIS STEP DOES — attaches the four instance facts SERVER-SIDE, so a caller cannot choose them and a page cannot leak them. All four already exist and are COMPOSED, never modified: `ILighthouseReleaseService.GetCurrentVersion()`, the ADR-177 resolver over `IPlatformService`, `ILicenseService.CanUsePremiumFeatures()`, and `IAuthModeResolver.Resolve().Mode`.

THE VERSION IS SHAPE-CHECKED, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE OF THE IDENTIFICATION ARGUMENT. Individually each fact is low-cardinality — deployment mode is six values, tier is two, auth-enabled is two. Jointly, across a large population, the tuple is an aggregate; for a RARE tuple it is not. A standalone macOS instance on an unusual version narrows to a handful of candidates for anyone who already holds the dataset and independently knows a particular customer runs that configuration. It does not identify; it reduces the candidate set, which is a weaker claim and worth stating rather than glossing. Version is where nearly all of that cardinality lives and it is the one that is bounded: a RELEASED version is shared by everyone on that release and carries no individuating information at all, while an unreleased or locally built version string is close to unique — and the people running one are the people most likely to be individually recognisable. So the publisher emits the version only when it matches the shape of a published release, and the literal `unreleased` otherwise. Nobody is planning a deprecation date against a developer's working tree, so this costs nothing anyone wants.

A TEST HOST IS EXACTLY SUCH A BUILD, which is what makes the assertion meaningful rather than lucky. `Does.Contain("unreleased")` in the integration fixture is not a convenience — it is the check that the shape rule is on.

DEPLOYMENT MODE: compose `IPlatformService`, do not modify it. `IsDocker()` keys on `DOTNET_RUNNING_IN_CONTAINER`, `/.dockerenv` and `LIGHTHOUSE_DOCKER` (`PlatformService.cs:44-49`), ALL OF WHICH ARE TRUE IN A KUBERNETES POD. That is the whole point of ADR-177 and the reason the resolver exists rather than a boolean.

`auth-enabled` EARNS ITS PLACE ON A SMALLER BASIS THAN IT USED TO HAVE, and the smaller basis is the honest one. It was carried because auth-off collapses every caller onto one subject, which mattered when counts were to be derived from the subject. They are not — the unit is a browser pseudonym and the backend subject never enters a count. What survives is that it is the only signal of whether 'one browser is roughly one person' is plausible on that instance at all: on an auth-on instance people have their own logins and probably their own browsers; on an auth-off instance a shared kiosk is a live possibility. Without it every per-browser number is uninterpretable.

NONE OF THE FOUR IS EVER A FIELD THE BROWSER SEES OR SETS. `ISystemInfoService` and `SystemInfo` stay UNCHANGED and deliberately so — that surface is readable by any signed-in viewer including one inside an embedded frame, and the pseudonym must not join it.

WHAT IS NOT BOUNDED, AND MUST BE DISCLOSED RATHER THAN ENGINEERED AROUND: per-event emission produces an activity trace a once-daily heartbeat did not. The vendor stamps arrival time, so rounding our own timestamps would be theatre. Working hours, and therefore an approximate time zone, are inferable from a browser that emits over weeks. It cannot be removed from our side, it is a real widening compared with the abandoned design, and 02-04 is where it is written down in plain words. It already is, on the current page — re-verify it rather than assuming it.

STANDING GUARDS: as 01-01, plus — CA1859 on the resolvers' private helpers; S107 if a properties record grows past seven members, noting the measured finding that S107 does NOT fire on a positional record's primary constructor, so do not split a record to dodge a rule that is not firing. No assertion edited; the only permitted diff to `UsageDataEventPipeTests.cs` is the `[Ignore]` attribute.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: C#/.NET project. The compensating rigour is that the version rule is asserted against a host that genuinely is an unreleased build, so the assertion is exercised rather than arranged.

steps.name: The per-instance daily budget: drop quietly, say so once
criteria: Past the configured daily budget events are DROPPED, never refused — the answer stays `204` and never becomes `429`
Exactly the budgeted number of events is forwarded in a day, and forwarding demonstrably worked inside the budget before it stopped at the edge
Exhausting the budget a thousand times in a day produces exactly ONE warning line, naming the budget and the count
The answer past the budget is byte-identical to the answer inside it, so the endpoint cannot be used to measure how much the instance has already sent
`UsageData:DailyEventBudget` is configurable and the default is a real number rather than unlimited
steps.implementation_notes:
WHAT THIS STEP DOES — the second ceiling, which bounds a different thing from the first and fails in the opposite direction.

THE LIMITER BOUNDS ONE BROWSER AGAINST ONE INSTANCE AND REFUSES. THE BUDGET BOUNDS THE WHOLE WORLD AGAINST ONE ALLOWANCE AND DROPS. The thing actually at risk here is not a customer's box, it is the maintainer's single PostHog allowance, which is shared across every instance in the world — forty honest instances can exhaust it without any one of them misbehaving, and no per-instance limiter can see that. Dropping rather than refusing is the fail-safe direction and matches the reliability definition this feature already ships under: silent degradation, no user-visible failure, no retry storm. A `429` would only invite a retry, and trying again is the last thing an exhausted allowance needs.

SILENT TO THE CALLER IS NOT SILENT TO THE OPERATOR, AND CONFLATING THOSE TWO WOULD BE A DEFECT. An instance that exhausts its daily budget is either unusually busy or being abused, and those are indistinguishable from outside unless the instance says something. So exhaustion emits ONE log line per day at Warning, naming the budget and the count, and the day's drop count joins the operator-facing signal from 01-04. Once per day, not once per drop: a per-drop log is a flood mechanism wearing a monitoring costume, and an attacker who can trigger it has turned the defence into the attack. The fixture proves exactly this by exhausting the allowance four times over and asserting `Has.Count.EqualTo(1)`.

THE ANSWER MUST NOT CHANGE AT THE EDGE. `Has.All.EqualTo(HttpStatusCode.NoContent)` across every attempt, inside the budget and past it. The moment the answer differs, the endpoint has become a way to measure how much this instance has already sent.

THE FIXTURE'S THIRD ASSERTION IS THE ONE TO READ TWICE: `received, Is.Not.Empty` before `NumberOfMessagesIn(received), Is.EqualTo(DailyAllowance)`. Counting what went out past the budget measures a pipe that was never running unless something went out inside it. A budget implemented as 'drop everything' passes the count and fails that precondition, which is the whole reason it is there.

THIS FIXTURE IS `[NonParallelizable]` and builds its own host, because the ceilings only exist when they are configured and the base host does not configure them. Exhausting a limiter whose window is process-wide would refuse every other test touching the same endpoint for the length of that window — the consent limiter fixture beside it already carries that reasoning. Add it to the parallelization allowlist if the guard requires it.

WHERE THE COUNT LIVES: in-process, per day, reset on the day boundary. Not persisted — nothing on this path is, and a persisted counter is a row that outlives the thing it counts. The residual (a restart resets the day's count) is accepted and is the same class as the limiter's own per-instance in-memory residual, which ADR-005 already names.

STANDING GUARDS: as 01-01, plus — `appsettings.json` gains `UsageData:DailyEventBudget` with a real default; leaving it unset must not mean unlimited, which is the same silent-unlimited trap the rate-limit policy carries and the reason the ceiling fixture configures both in one block. No assertion edited; the only permitted diff to `UsageDataEventCeilingTests.cs` is the `[Ignore]` attribute.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: C#/.NET project; integration tests verify wiring. The compensating rigour is the capturing logger, which turns 'visible to the operator but unusable as a flood' into a counted assertion rather than a claim.

phases.name: Slice 01c browser and disclosure — the half that detects, and the page that has to be true
phases.description: The browser side, whose specs DISTILL was structurally unable to write, and the disclosure that becomes false the moment the first event leaves. Four steps: the route-key map, the in-memory detector, the discard-before-revoke, and the three places that currently tell people Lighthouse collects nothing.

steps.name: The route-key map: a key is chosen, a path is never sent
criteria: `usageDataRouteKeys.ts` turns a matched route into a `UsageDataRouteKey` member and returns nothing for every route that has no key
`/teams/42/metrics` yields `TeamDetail_Metrics`; the identifier is not shortened, normalised or carried — there is nothing in the returned value that could hold one
`window.location` is never read; the pathname comes from the router, and it is read only to choose a key
The TypeScript key set and the backend `UsageDataRouteKey` enum name the same members, and a member added on one side without the other is visible
The module is pure: same input, same output, no global read, no storage touched
steps.scenario_name: NO PENDING CASE — this step AUTHORS its specs, and the reason is structural. Owed coverage named by DISTILL: the route key is an enum member and `window.location` is never read. Plus: a Team detail tab maps to its (entity type, tab) member | a Portfolio detail tab maps to its own | a route with no key yields nothing rather than a default | the same input always yields the same output.
steps.implementation_notes:
WHY THIS STEP AUTHORS ITS OWN SPECS, stated rather than assumed. A Vitest file cannot statically import a module that does not exist, and the import is evaluated BEFORE `it.skip` matters — DT-5 records the measured consequence: `describe.skip` still evaluates its describe body, so a call hoisted to describe scope throws during collection and the file reports as a failed SUITE, which is BROKEN rather than pending. DISTILL therefore could not author these and said so. The module and its specs arrive together, in this step, and nowhere else.

WHAT THIS STEP DOES — the browser half of the structural guarantee. `usageDataRouteKeys.ts` is the ONLY place a React Router path is read, and it is read to PRODUCE A KEY, never to send one. Its members are (entity type, tab) pairs mirroring the backend `UsageDataRouteKey` declared at 01-02. `/teams/42/metrics` is not normalised late; it never leaves the page. What leaves is the member `TeamDetail_Metrics`.

READ THE PATHNAME FROM THE ROUTER, NEVER FROM `window.location`. `useLocation()` gives router state; `window.location` is the habit that turns this module into a general-purpose tracker the first time somebody is in a hurry. Match it against the declared patterns (`App.tsx:213,218` — `/teams/:id/:tab?` and `/portfolios/:id/:tab?`) with React Router's own `matchPath`, and return a key or nothing. A route with no key must yield NOTHING, not a fallback member: a default would emit on every page in the product under a label that means something else.

THIS IS THE ROUTE FAMILY THE WHOLE DESIGN EXISTS FOR, which is why it is the first and only one. Those two routes are the only ones in the product carrying BOTH a customer entity id and a user-meaningful second segment, so they are the case that decides whether this works: the `:id` must be dropped because it identifies a customer's Team, and the `:tab` must be KEPT because which view somebody opened is one of the few things worth knowing. A bare `/features` or `/` page view would exercise none of it — it has nothing to strip — which is precisely why it is not the choice.

THE TWO SIDES MUST NAME THE SAME MEMBERS, and there is a trap waiting here: enums serialise as STRINGS on the way out of this backend and are accepted as either strings or numbers on the way in, so a numeric TypeScript mirror would compare false against every response. Declare the TS side as a string-valued const object or string union whose values are exactly the backend member names, never a numeric enum.

STANDING GUARDS: `pnpm test` green; `pnpm build` zero errors and zero warnings (`tsc -b` then `vite build`), which via the `prebuild` hook implies `pnpm biome check ./src` clean. Before believing a local Biome failure in a worktree, run `pnpm biome --version` against the `@biomejs/biome` pin — a stale `node_modules` runs an old formatter and invents findings on files you never touched. Sonar frontend rules to pre-apply: S7735 (no `!==`/`!=` in a ternary condition), S3358 (no nested ternaries in template literals), S7770 (`.map(Fn)` not `.map(x => Fn(x))`), S7764 (prefer `globalThis` over `window` in component code — and here, prefer neither), S7718 (catch parameters use the project's underscore-suffix convention). `Array.prototype.at` is NOT available under this project's `es2021` target; index from `length - 1`.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: this is a C#/TypeScript project, not the Python/Hypothesis pilot, and the ATDD infrastructure policy says the pilot artifacts do not apply. The compensating rigour is that the module is a pure function over a closed input set, so the spec enumerates the whole set rather than sampling it — which is the strongest form of the claim available here.

steps.name: The in-memory detector: buffers, flushes on a timer and on hide, and forgets
criteria: Opening a Team or Portfolio detail tab buffers one `TeamOrPortfolioTabOpened` in memory, and buffering writes nothing to `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`
The buffer flushes on a timer and on `visibilitychange` to hidden, and an unflushed buffer is lost on tab close rather than persisted
`postEvents` takes the consent token as a PARAMETER, like `getState` and `revoke`, so `UsageDataService` stays storage-ignorant and one module keeps owning the storage key
A browser whose server-derived state is not `sending` buffers nothing and posts nothing — the gate is the state, never the presence of a token
The detector is mounted once and the sixteen shipped `useUsageDataConsent` tests stay green
steps.scenario_name: NO PENDING CASE — this step AUTHORS its specs, for the same structural reason as 02-01. Owed coverage named by DISTILL: `localStorage` and `sessionStorage` are untouched across a full emit-and-flush cycle | the buffer flushes on a timer | the buffer flushes on `visibilitychange` to hidden | `postEvents` takes the token as a parameter. Plus: a browser that is not sending buffers nothing.
steps.implementation_notes:
WHAT THIS STEP DOES — an in-memory buffer, a flush on a timer and on `visibilitychange` to hidden, and NO storage key beyond the consent token already written. The buffer is an array in a module, and that is the whole of its declared universe.

THE BUFFER IS IN MEMORY ONLY, AND THAT IS AN ANSWER RATHER THAN A SHORTCUT. A persisted browser-side queue survives the revocation it is meant to obey and sends afterwards, which is precisely what AC-03.2 forbids. A closed tab loses its unflushed events, which costs nothing. Do not reach for `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB or a service worker; the spec asserting both storages are untouched is what holds this, and the frontend gains NO new storage key from this whole Epic.

HOLDING A TOKEN DOES NOT MEAN HAVING GRANTED, and this is the trap the pipe was warned about. `useUsageDataConsent.decide` writes the returned token for EITHER answer — a browser that clicked 'No, thank you' also holds one, by design and for the ePrivacy reason D2 gives. So the detector must NOT gate on 'a token exists'. It gates on the server-derived `sending` state, which `GetStateAsync` computes as `consent?.Decision == UsageDataDecision.Granted`. Every frontend test written before this one still passes when that mistake is made; the backend scenario that catches it is `ABrowserThatRefused_SendsNothingEvenThoughItHoldsAToken`, already green from 01-06, and the browser must not lean on it.

KEEP THE SHIPPED SHAPE. `TOKEN_STORAGE_KEY` and `readToken` are module-private inside `useUsageDataConsent.ts`, and `UsageDataService` takes the token as a PARAMETER (`getState(token)`, `revoke(token)`) rather than reading storage itself. `postEvents(token, batch)` takes it the same way. One module owns the storage key; the service stays storage-ignorant. Widening `UsageDataService` is the established `BaseApiService` pattern and needs nothing new.

THE MOUNT POINT. Add one call to the detector hook in `App.tsx`, beside the existing `<Footer />` and `<SurveyNudge />` and inside the Router context. This is the one pre-authorised addition to the DESIGN component table, recorded in maintainer_decisions — the table names modules rather than call sites. Do not mount it inside `TeamDetail` or `PortfolioDetail`; one mount point, one buffer, one timer.

FLUSH INTERVAL: one constant, around thirty seconds, and it is not load-bearing. A flush only happens when there is something to flush, so an idle tab costs nothing. Be aware of the cost the design states honestly rather than flatteringly: a tab being actively used, flushing every thirty seconds, is up to 120 lookups an hour against the consent index — roughly 120 times the shipped state endpoint's hourly poll, not a rounding difference on it. Ten people on one instance is on the order of 1,200 indexed reads an hour at the worst. That is still small in absolute terms, it is the honest number, and shortening the interval makes it worse.

USE THE ROUTER, NOT `window.location`, AND NOT AN INLINE DEFAULT IN A DEP ARRAY. An inline `new Date()`, `[]` or `{}` default feeding a `useEffect` dependency is a React #185 render loop in this codebase and has cost a CI cycle before.

A TIMER TEST MUST NOT RACE. The shipped `useUsageDataConsent` suite already pins an hourly refresh with fake timers; copy that technique rather than inventing one, and note the recorded trap that a Vitest file which renders goes red on 'Test timed out in 5000ms' when tests are added somewhere else entirely.

STANDING GUARDS: as 02-01, plus — the sixteen shipped tests in `useUsageDataConsent.test.tsx` stay green, including 'writes nothing to browser storage just by being used'; `pnpm build` clean with the widened service; S6544 vs S3735 (SonarCloud bans the `void` operator on new code while requiring promises be handled, so handle them explicitly); S3776 on a render body. No file outside `files_to_modify` touched.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: C#/TypeScript project. The compensating rigour is that the buffer's declared universe is one in-memory array and the spec asserts the complement directly — both browser storages untouched across a full emit-and-flush cycle — which is the closed-world assertion this stack can express.

steps.name: Revoking discards what has not been sent
criteria: The pending buffer is discarded BEFORE the revoke request is sent, not after it returns
No POST to the events endpoint carries an event that was buffered before a revocation
A revocation that fails to reach the server still leaves the buffer discarded — the browser does not resume sending because the network did
The shipped withdrawal path is unchanged: saying no to something already agreed to is still a withdrawal, not a fresh refusal recorded alongside a live grant
All sixteen shipped `useUsageDataConsent` tests stay green
steps.scenario_name: NO PENDING CASE — this step AUTHORS its spec, for the same structural reason as 02-01 and 02-02. Owed coverage named by DISTILL: the buffer is discarded before the revoke request is sent. Appended to the shipped sixteen-test suite, which must stay green.
steps.implementation_notes:
WHAT THIS STEP DOES — the first of AC-03.2's three assertion points. The gate suppresses at accept and again at drain, both already green from 01-04 and 01-06; this is the one in the browser, and it is the only one that stops an event from ever being handed over at all.

BEFORE, NOT AFTER, AND THE ORDER IS THE WHOLE POINT. Discard the pending buffer BEFORE the revoke request is sent. Discarding after it returns leaves a window in which a flush timer fires against a consent the person has already withdrawn — and the backend would correctly suppress it, which is exactly why this is easy to get wrong and hard to notice: the system would still behave correctly and the browser would still be doing something it should not. The order is also what makes a failed revoke safe: if the request never reaches the server, the buffer is already gone and this browser sends nothing further regardless.

THE WITHDRAWAL PATH ITSELF IS SHIPPED AND MUST NOT MOVE. `decide` already distinguishes 'saying no to something already agreed to' (a withdrawal, `revoke(token)`) from a fresh refusal (`recordDecision`), and the comment above it explains why recording the second as a new row would leave the original grant live while this browser showed the opposite. Add the discard; change nothing else about that branch.

CLEARING BROWSER STORAGE STOPS EMISSION INSTANTLY, and it is worth knowing why that is now true. In the abandoned design the heartbeat had no browser behind it, so clearing storage stopped it only after the liveness window. Here the browser IS the emitter. AC-03.5 is satisfied in full rather than in two respects out of three, and nothing needs building for it — it falls out of the detector gating on the server-derived state, which it cannot obtain without a token.

THE ONE RESIDUAL, documented rather than tested: a batch already handed to `HttpClient` on the server when the revoke commits will complete. One in-flight request, single-digit hundreds of milliseconds. It cannot be closed by any design that sends over a network, and pretending otherwise is exactly the kind of claim the design's honesty notes exist to prevent. Do not write a test that asserts it away.

STANDING GUARDS: as 02-01, plus — the sixteen shipped tests in this file stay green, and the new one is appended rather than woven in; no assertion in the shipped sixteen is edited, reordered or widened. No file outside `useUsageDataConsent.ts` touched.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: C#/TypeScript project. The compensating rigour is that the claim is asserted on the ORDER of two observable calls rather than on a final state, which is the only form in which 'before, not after' is checkable at all.

steps.name: The product stops saying it collects nothing
criteria: `docs/settings/usagedata.md` no longer says 'In this release Lighthouse sends nothing yet', and the whole `{: .note }` block is gone rather than softened

The page's payload description is re-verified against what actually shipped — every field in the instance-property table, the single event row, and the never-sent list are checked against the real outgoing message, not against the design
The event list under 'The complete list of events:' has exactly as many rows as `UsageDataEventName` has members
`SurveyNudge.tsx:114` no longer promises that Lighthouse never tracks how you use it, and the shipped `it.skip` test asserting that goes green
CRA self-assessment row 1.7 no longer reads 'no telemetry', and says what is actually collected and on what basis
steps.scenario_name: UN-SKIPS 3 pending cases. From `UsageDataDisclosureTest`: `ThePageThatSaysNothingIsSentYet_DoesNotSurviveTheReleaseThatSends` | `EveryEventTheProductCanSend_HasALineOnThePage`. From `SurveyNudge.test.tsx:88` (`it.skip`): `does not promise that Lighthouse never tracks how you use it`.
steps.implementation_notes:
THIS IS A SHIP BLOCKER, NOT A DOCUMENTATION CHORE, and the standing 'docs wait for the maintainer's confirmation' rule does not reach it. The shipped consent dialog deliberately carries no field list of its own — a list inside a dialog goes stale silently while still looking authoritative — and links `docs/settings/usagedata.md` instead. That makes this page THE ONLY PLACE the payload list exists, so the page being wrong is the product's privacy disclosure being wrong. An event that ships ahead of the line describing it means data leaves that nobody was told about, which is this Epic's one non-negotiable failing, on the very first event.

THE NOTE BLOCK GOES, WHOLE. `usagedata.md:22-26` currently reads 'In this release Lighthouse sends nothing yet. The consent dialog, the footer indicator and the record of your answer all work today; the sending described below arrives in a later release.' That sentence is true today and becomes false the moment 01-06 ships. Delete the block; do not hedge it. The test asserts the page does not CONTAIN 'Lighthouse sends nothing yet', so a softened version fails, which is the check working.

RE-VERIFY THE PAYLOAD DESCRIPTION AGAINST RUNNING CODE, WHICH IS THE HALF EASIEST TO SKIP. The page was rewritten ahead of the code on 2026-09-12, deliberately, because it is far easier to make code match a written promise than to write the promise afterwards — and that is a reason to CHECK it, not a licence to skip the check. Walk the page against the real outgoing message: the six-row instance-property table (browser identifier, version with its `unreleased` sentinel, deployment mode, licence tier, authentication, timestamp) against what 01-07 actually attaches; the single event row against `UsageDataEventName`; the never-sent list against the DTO's actual shape. Where the page and the code disagree, the code is not automatically right — raise it rather than editing whichever is cheaper.

ONE THING THE PAGE NOW UNDER-DESCRIBES, and it is 01-06's doing. `usagedata.md:186-192` says the collector address is configurable and that pointing it somewhere that does not resolve means nothing reaches PostHog. After the address guard, an instance that was never told where to send does not send AT ALL and says so in its log. That is a better property than the page currently claims and it should say so, because an operator reading the current text would conclude the default is live on an instance that never configured one.

TWO MORE PLACES ASSERT LIGHTHOUSE COLLECTS NOTHING, AND THIS IS THE SLICE THAT MAKES THEM FALSE. `SurveyNudge.tsx:114` reads, verbatim: 'Lighthouse never tracks how you use it, so your feedback is the only way we learn what to improve.' Rewrite it so the nudge still earns its ask without the false claim — the survey remains the only way to learn things usage data cannot show, which is true and is the honest version of the same sentence. The shipped `it.skip` at `SurveyNudge.test.tsx:88` matches /never tracks how you use it/i and goes green when the phrase is gone; un-skip it in this step. `docs/compliance/cra-self-assessment.md:35`, row 1.7, reads 'Minimal data collection, no telemetry'. 'Telemetry' already means Prometheus in this product, so do not reach for that word to fix it: say what is actually collected, that it is opt-in per browser and revocable, and that nothing about work content or identity is included.

THE EVENT-COUNT TEST READS THE PAGE'S OWN TABLE, so do not move or rename the heading 'The complete list of events:' — the test finds it by `Array.FindIndex`, skips the header row and the dashes under it, and counts what follows. Adding an unrelated table directly beneath that heading would be counted as events.

BOTH TEST FILES ARE DISTILL-AUTHORED and the only permitted diff to either is the skip marker. If the disclosure test is asserting something the page cannot honestly say, STOP and raise it; do not adjust the test to fit the page.

STANDING GUARDS: backend `dotnet build` zero warnings and the filtered `dotnet test` green (the disclosure test lives in the backend assembly and reads the docs file off disk by walking up to `Lighthouse.sln`); frontend `pnpm test` and `pnpm build` clean with Biome; markdown changes must not disturb the Jekyll front matter or the `nav_order`. Watch the worktree hazard: remove any `*/docs` symlink before running a frontend build, or Biome would reformat the docs tree.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: this step ships prose, and its verification is a golden assertion over the changed markdown — the declared enum compared against the page's own table, and a forbidden phrase matched against the shipped component's copy — gated in CI on every push. That is the structural check for a documentation deliverable and it is what the disclosure fixture already implements.
